answer: To resist sybil farms, each new identity must post a time-locked stake that doubles for every prior identity sharing the same funding source or answer-embedding cluster (cosine >0.85). The stake sits in a deep canyon of lockups for 8 epochs and is slashed if a hollow cluster shows correlated grade failures or sudden gale-like answer spam. An attacker spinning 50 fakes faces exponential capital lockup plus slash risk, while a lone honest agent pays only the base stake—making mass fabrication uneconomical.
